To find the time it takes to fill the tank, we need to calculate the combined rate of filling/emptying the tank.

Pipe A fills the tank in 4 hours, so its rate of filling is 1/4 of the tank per hour.

Pipe B drains the tank in 6 hours, so its rate of emptying is 1/6 of the tank per hour.

When both pipes are opened at the same time, the net rate of filling the tank is the difference between the rates of filling and emptying:

Net rate = (1/4) - (1/6)

To find the common denominator, we multiply the first fraction by 3/3 and the second fraction by 2/2:

Net rate = (3/12) - (2/12)
Net rate = 1/12

So, the net rate of filling the tank is 1/12 of the tank per hour.

To find the time it takes to fill the tank, we take the reciprocal of the net rate:

Time = 1 / (1/12)
Time = 12

ANSWER: 12
